summary: Best-evidenced answer to 'Kutchi or Gujarati at home?': contested, most likely a Kutchi-Gujarati continuum. For: one East Africa language survey (AwaaZ/ResearchGate, drawing on Neale 1974) lists 'Cutchi-speaking Leva Patel (Hindu)'. Against: Wikipedia says Hindu Kutchi groups in East Africa use Gujarati, and that Hindus of rural-Kutch descent 'reject Kutchi' and speak Gujaratised Kutchi (e.g. 'chhado hane' for 'chhodo have'). The SKLPC diaspora school teaches Gujarati. Kutch district (2011) is 55% Gujarati and 34% Kutchi, and eastern Kutchi is converging on Gujarati. Practical read: grammar varies by speaker and generation, but Kutchi words and verb forms (achanto/vinanto 'coming/going', aaun 'I', aain polite 'you', koro 'what', kien 'how', achija 'bye') carry the community flavour. Every Kutchi form here is 'claimed' or thinly 'verified' from snippets, because page fetches were blocked, and much grammar comes from Khoja or Memon sources. Confirm with SKLPC native speakers before teaching.

features.english: I am coming / I am going
features.note: The Wikipedia table gives both columns (tagged 'citation needed'). Memeraki independently supports the stems ach- (come) and van- (go): 'Aain achota' = are you coming, 'Kada vanota' = where are you going. The Kutchi form has no separate 'chhun'-type auxiliary; the -nto/-ota ending carries tense. That last point is an observation from these examples, not a sourced rule. gaps: No source names the home language of Kutch Leva Patels in Kutch itself. East African evidence conflicts (AwaaZ/ResearchGate: Cutchi-speaking Leva Patels; Wikipedia: Hindus use Gujarati / 'reject Kutchi'). Native-speaker confirmation from SKLPC members is required.

WebFetch was blocked by the session network policy for every host tried (cal.org, wikipedia.org, freelang.net, glottolog.org, archive.org, panjokutch.com). The CAL heritage PDF, FreeLang Kutchi dictionary, Glottolog and Grierson LSI vol. VIII pt. I (Sindhi incl. Kachchhi, 1919) were therefore NOT read; all evidence comes from search snippets. Allow these domains and re-run.
Grierson LSI: Kachchhi specimens are in vol. VIII pt. I (archive.org/details/in.gov.ignca.23432; dsal.uchicago.edu/books/lsi/); Kathiawadi is in the Gujarati volume (IX pt. II). Neither was read.

Not found in Kutchi: copula paradigm, negation, past and future tense, 'why', and everyday words eat, drink, food, home, good, today, tomorrow. 'maani' = roti is attested for Sindhi only, not confirmed for Kutchi.
No academic thesis on Kutch-variety Gujarati phonology or morphology surfaced. The Gujarati dialect chain-shift papers (2022/2023) cover Kathiawadi, Surti, Charotari and Pattani, not Kutch.
Most Kutchi grammar evidence comes from Khoja (Ismaili Muslim) or Memon sources; Hindu-farming-caste Kutchi is undocumented.
Neale (1974) 'Language use among the Asian communities' (Kenya) and Bharati (1972) on Patels and Lohanas are primary sources worth obtaining.
Standard-Gujarati glosses marked 'mine' in phrase notes are textbook forms supplied for pairing and were not source-checked this session.
